pack.description: French-English false friends: English words that look like a French word but mean something else, with the trap and the correct translation.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of the false friends most likely to cause errors for French speakers in academic and campus English; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: used to say what is really true, often when it is surprising or different from what was said
entries.example_academic: The reform actually increased costs, contrary to what its designers expected.
entries.example_spoken: I actually liked the lecture more than I expected.

entries.definition: in the end, after a long time or a lot of effort
entries.example_academic: The species eventually spread across the entire continent.
entries.example_spoken: We eventually found the room after asking three people.

entries.definition: a building or room where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow
entries.example_academic: The library holds one of the largest collections of medieval manuscripts in the country.
entries.example_spoken: I'll be at the library until it closes.

entries.definition: a talk given to a group of students to teach them about a subject
entries.example_academic: The lecture introduced the main theories of economic growth.
entries.example_spoken: I missed the lecture; can I copy your notes?

entries.definition: showing good judgment; reasonable and practical
entries.example_academic: A sensible precaution would be to repeat the measurement with a second instrument.
entries.example_spoken: It's sensible to start the essay a week early.

entries.definition: to go to and be present at an event, class or meeting
entries.example_academic: More than three hundred delegates attended the conference.
entries.example_spoken: I can't attend the review session tomorrow.

entries.definition: to help someone to do something
entries.example_academic: Volunteers assisted the researchers in collecting samples.
entries.example_spoken: The tutor will assist you with the lab report.

entries.definition: to begin again after stopping for a time
entries.example_academic: Trade resumed once the border reopened.
entries.example_spoken: Classes resume on Monday after the break.

entries.definition: to behave as if something is true when you know it is not
entries.example_academic: Some birds pretend to be injured in order to lead predators away from their young.
entries.example_spoken: He pretended to be asleep when I came in.

entries.definition: to understand or become aware of something
entries.example_academic: Researchers soon realized that the two effects were connected.
entries.example_spoken: I just realized that I left my charger at home.

false_friend_fr.correct: réaliser un projet = to carry out, to achieve

entries.definition: a place where people study for a degree after high school
entries.example_academic: Nearly half of those who start college do not complete a degree within six years.
entries.example_spoken: My sister starts college in the fall.

false_friend_fr.correct: le collège = middle school, junior high school

entries.definition: an act of traveling from one place to another, especially over a long distance
entries.example_academic: The journey from the coast to the capital took traders nearly a month.
entries.example_spoken: The journey to campus takes me forty minutes.

entries.definition: a particular place or position
entries.example_academic: The location of the factory was determined by access to the river.
entries.example_spoken: The workshop has moved to a new location.

entries.definition: knowledge or skill gained from doing something, or something that happens to you
entries.example_academic: Candidates with experience of fieldwork were given priority.
entries.example_spoken: Do you have any experience with this software?

entries.definition: a possibility that something will happen; or an opportunity to do something
entries.example_academic: There is little chance that the species will recover without intervention.
entries.example_spoken: I didn't get a chance to ask my question.

false_friend_fr.correct: la chance = luck; avoir de la chance = to be lucky

entries.definition: a small group of words that form a unit of meaning, usually without a complete verb
entries.example_academic: The phrase "survival of the fittest" was not coined by Darwin.
entries.example_spoken: What does this phrase mean in the second line?

entries.definition: a period of time when something is late or has to wait
entries.example_academic: The delay in publishing the results was caused by a dispute over the data.
entries.example_spoken: Sorry for the delay in getting back to you.

false_friend_fr.correct: un délai = a deadline, a time limit

entries.definition: to pay no attention to something or someone on purpose
entries.translation_fr: ne pas tenir compte de, faire comme si on ne voyait pas
entries.example_academic: The model ignores the cost of transport.
entries.example_spoken: He ignored my message for three days.

false_friend_fr.correct: ignorer quelque chose = not to know something

entries.definition: showing that you understand and care about another person's problems
entries.example_academic: Readers are invited to take a sympathetic view of the main character's choices.
entries.example_spoken: My advisor was very sympathetic when I explained the situation.

entries.definition: including all or almost all the facts or parts of something
entries.example_academic: The report offers a comprehensive review of research published since 1990.
entries.example_spoken: The study guide is really comprehensive; it covers every chapter.

entries.definition: the act of making someone believe something that is not true
entries.example_academic: The experiment involved a mild deception: participants were not told its real purpose.
entries.example_spoken: It wasn't a mistake; it was deliberate deception.

entries.definition: an unfair opinion or feeling about a group, formed without enough knowledge
entries.example_academic: The study measured prejudice by comparing responses to identical applications.
entries.example_spoken: There's still a lot of prejudice against people with accents.

entries.definition: a medical doctor
entries.example_academic: Rural areas have far fewer physicians per inhabitant than cities.
entries.example_spoken: My physician told me to rest for a week.

entries.definition: a job that is available for someone to do; or a room that is free
entries.example_academic: The department advertised the vacancy in three international journals.
entries.example_spoken: There's a vacancy at the front desk if you want a job.

entries.definition: the state of being separate from other people, places or things
entries.example_academic: Geographic isolation allowed the island's species to evolve in unusual ways.
entries.example_spoken: Working from home can lead to a feeling of isolation.

entries.definition: able to be used for many purposes, or able to do many different things well
entries.example_academic: Bamboo is a versatile material used in construction, textiles and paper.
entries.example_spoken: She's a versatile player who can cover any position.

entries.definition: honest and direct, even when the truth is uncomfortable
entries.example_academic: The memoir gives a candid account of the negotiations.
entries.example_spoken: To be candid, I didn't like the first draft.

entries.definition: the wish to harm or upset other people
entries.example_academic: The court found no evidence of malice in the publication of the article.
entries.example_spoken: There was no malice in his joke; he just didn't think.

entries.definition: ordinary, dull and not interesting
entries.example_academic: Much of the archive consists of mundane records such as receipts and inventories.
entries.example_spoken: My part of the project is pretty mundane: checking references.

false_friend_fr.correct: mondain = fashionable, relating to high society

entries.definition: kind, helpful and generous, especially toward people with less power
entries.example_academic: The ruler is portrayed in the chronicle as a benevolent protector of the poor.
entries.example_spoken: He's a benevolent boss who really looks after the interns.

false_friend_fr.correct: un bénévole = a volunteer; bénévole (adj.) = voluntary, unpaid

entries.definition: of little importance or value
entries.example_academic: The differences between the two versions are trivial and do not affect the argument.
entries.example_spoken: It's a trivial mistake; just fix the date.

entries.definition: making you feel pity; or, informally, weak and useless in a way that deserves no respect
entries.example_academic: The letters paint a pathetic picture of soldiers abandoned without supplies.
entries.example_spoken: My first attempt at the proof was pathetic.

entries.definition: drunk; or very excited by something
entries.example_academic: Drivers found to be intoxicated lose their license for at least a year.
entries.example_spoken: He was clearly intoxicated, so we called him a taxi.

false_friend_fr.correct: intoxiqué = poisoned; une intoxication alimentaire = food poisoning

entries.definition: a substance added to food or other products to stop them from decaying
entries.example_academic: Salt was the most widely used preservative before refrigeration.
entries.example_spoken: This bread has no preservatives, so it won't last long.

entries.definition: friendly and cheerful
entries.example_academic: Colleagues remembered him as a genial host who welcomed visiting scholars.
entries.example_spoken: Our landlord is a genial man who always stops to chat.

entries.definition: causing fear or respect because of being very large, powerful or difficult
entries.example_academic: The mountains formed a formidable barrier to trade.
entries.example_spoken: She's a formidable opponent in any debate.

entries.definition: having people living there
entries.example_academic: The valley has been inhabited continuously for at least six thousand years.
entries.example_spoken: Is that island inhabited, or is it just birds?

entries.definition: giving very careful attention to detail; hard to please
entries.example_academic: A fastidious editor, she checked every quotation against its source.
entries.example_spoken: He's fastidious about his notes; everything is color-coded.

entries.definition: bad-tempered in a childish way, especially when you do not get what you want
entries.example_academic: The minister's petulant reply did little to calm his critics.
entries.example_spoken: Don't be petulant just because your idea wasn't chosen.

entries.definition: hopeful and confident about the future
entries.example_academic: Investors were less sanguine about the firm's prospects than its managers were.
entries.example_spoken: I'm not very sanguine about finishing by Friday.

entries.definition: agreement; or the fact of two things happening at the same time
entries.example_academic: The measure required the concurrence of both chambers.
entries.example_spoken: We can't change the date without the concurrence of the whole group.

entries.definition: to show a feeling or quality clearly
entries.example_academic: The early letters evince a growing impatience with court politics.
entries.example_spoken: He evinced no interest at all in the group project.

false_friend_fr.correct: évincer = to oust, to push out

entries.definition: skill at inventing things and solving problems in clever new ways
entries.example_academic: The irrigation system is a testament to the ingenuity of its builders.
entries.example_spoken: It took some ingenuity to fit everything into one slide.

entries.definition: aggressive, easily annoyed and ready to argue
entries.example_academic: The delegation adopted a truculent tone that made compromise unlikely.
entries.example_spoken: He gets truculent whenever someone questions his data.

false_friend_fr.correct: truculent (fr) = colorful, earthy, larger than life

entries.definition: having a strong but not usually lasting feeling of love or enthusiasm for someone or something
entries.example_academic: Investors became infatuated with any company that mentioned the new technology.
entries.example_spoken: He's completely infatuated with that band.

false_friend_fr.correct: infatué (de soi-même) = conceited, full of oneself
